question: Is the LIVE co-coverage graph sparse enough for peer_eq to carry graph information, or has it collapsed into cross-sectional demeaning?
why_it_was_asked: An end-to-end integration run on 23 real names returned corr(peer_eq, own_ret) = -1.000 exactly. That is the signature of a COMPLETE graph, where peer_eq_i = (S - r_i)/(n-1) is a strictly decreasing function of own return.
reading: Every major brokerage covers every mega-cap, so co-coverage is UNIVERSAL and therefore uninformative: it cannot say which names are related because it says all of them are. peer_eq then ranks names exactly in reverse order of their own return — short-horizon reversal, which this programme has Holm-surviving evidence AGAINST. The output is not a weak selector, it is a harmful one.
why_the_screen_could_not_see_it: The screen ran on thousands of CRSP names where a median ANALYST covers 4 firms, so an edge was selective and meant something. AMENDMENT-3 showed firm-level attribution survives — but on that same large universe, where a firm graph is still sparse RELATIVE TO ITS SIZE. A 179-name mega-cap universe is the one setting where the mechanism cannot work.
why_sparsifying_does_not_rescue_it: Requiring more shared brokerages reduces the correlation only around 8-12 shared firms, by which point 11-45% of the universe is unrankable. More decisively, 'an edge requires 10 shared brokerages' is NOT the mechanism the screen validated: `peer_shared` (count-weighted edges) was an arm there and did NOT beat `peer_eq`. There is no evidence for the sparsified variant.
what_would_make_it_work: A universe whose coverage is SELECTIVE — mid and small caps, where a name is followed by a handful of brokers rather than all of them. That is a universe change, not a parameter change, and it needs its own declaration.
guard: graph_propagation.assert_graph_informative refuses above 60% edge density or |corr with own return| > 0.25.
